title: design tree
description: The plan of a piece of work, at .rn/<yyyymmdd>-<goal>/design-tree.json: the goal, and the deliverables in the order of the work, each with the intents of its best practice in that best practice's order, each intent with its decisions. It keeps only what holds now, and git keeps the history of each point.

goal.description: The one end the user is after, which every deliverable serves.

decided.description: The end, as one sentence with the user as its subject.

deliverables.description: Every deliverable the goal needs, in the order of the work, each after the deliverables its inputs and preconditions name. A research deliverable comes before the decisions it serves, and a meta deliverable before the first deliverable of its kind, each at the top level. A research deliverable reads like this: `{"name": "The planner knows how plugins hand a task to a subagent", "path": ".rn/20261107-rn/research/subagents.md", "kind": "research", "inputs": [], "preconditions": [], "status": "open", "intents": []}`, and a later deliverable names its path in inputs.

by.description: Who settled the point. user: the user decided it. maker: the maker of the deliverable decided it, such as `{"about": "The figure's form", "decided": "The README shows the flow as a Mermaid sequence", "by": "maker"}`. reasoning: it follows from the goal and the best practices. research: a source found it. The reason itself goes in the commit message that makes the decision.

name.description: The one thing that holds toward the goal once the deliverable exists, so that the user knows where the work stands without opening it. It leaves out the path and the kind, which have fields of their own.

path.description: Where the deliverable lies, from the top of the repository: a file, or a folder for a deliverable of many files.

kind.description: The name of the folder of the best practice whose intents the deliverable meets, such as readme.

done.description: A deliverable that meets every intent of its best practice. It keeps one line, its name, path, kind, and status, as its decisions now hold in the deliverable itself.

status.description: done: the deliverable meets every intent of its best practice.

open.description: A deliverable not yet done, with the intents of its best practice and the decisions that answer them.

inputs.description: The path of each deliverable this one takes its content from, each of a kind that its best practice names in inputs. A path may name a file outside the tree that already exists, such as `["docs/api.md"]` for a README of an API that the work doesn't change. The list stays empty where the deliverable takes none.

preconditions.description: The path of each deliverable whose result this one needs passed before it starts, a deliverable of each kind that its best practice names in preconditions among them, such as the code that a README describes, and the meta deliverable of its own kind where the tree holds one. The list stays empty where the deliverable needs none.

status.description: Where the deliverable stands. open: no work on it has started. doing: someone is making it, which starts only once each of its preconditions has the status done or is a best practice that waits only on its example.

intents.description: Each intent of the deliverable's best practice, in that best practice's order.

intent.description: One intent of the best practice, with whether the deliverable meets it and the decisions that answer it.

id.description: The intent's ID in its best practice, such as Q1.

good.description: true once the deliverable meets the intent, false until then.

decisions.description: The decisions that answer the intent, each settled once its inputs exist. The list stays empty until a point of the intent comes up.

about.description: The point of the intent that the decision settles, in a few words.

unsettled.description: A point still open, which the maker asks about instead of guessing.

decided.description: null while the point is open.
